text:
B: Hi, Hira, is it? I'm Luke. Third call, we're practically pros now.
A: Hello. Yes, Hira. I think so, yes.
B: Where are you based?
A: Reading. Earley.
B: Oh nice, I'm in Bristol, so we're just down the M4 from each other, sort of. I see you've got a lot of books behind you. Are those library ones?
A: Some of them. The thick ones are for work. The others are from Reading library.
B: What are you reading at the moment? I'm always nosing at people's shelves.
A: Erm, a crime novel. A Japanese one, translated. I like translated fiction quite a lot.
B: Oh, brilliant, which one? I did a month in Japan a few years ago, so I'm a bit obsessed. I'm forever going on about it, sorry.
A: The Devotion of Suspect X. Do you know it?
B: Yes! The maths teacher one. That's so good, isn't it, the twist. There's a film of it too, I think, a Korean one as well, maybe. I watch a lot of that stuff at the Watershed here.
A: I didn't know there was a film. I'd like to go to Japan one day. Not soon, but one day.
B: You should, honestly. Kyoto in the autumn is ridiculous. Anyway, what do you do? Sorry, I've just launched straight into books.
A: No, it's fine. I work in a hospital pharmacy. On the wards.
B: Oh, wow, that's proper responsibility. I'm an exec assistant, so my big crisis is the MD double-booking a lunch.
A: That is also a problem. Just a different kind.
B: Ha, thank you, I'll tell him you said that. Do you like it, the hospital?
A: Yes. It's a lot of checking, but I like the patients. Many are older, and some only speak Punjabi or Urdu, so I can help with that.
B: That must make such a difference for them, being able to actually understand what they're taking.
A: Yes, I think so. They relax more.
B: Yeah. What do you do to switch off? I do parkrun and I cook, mostly Korean stuff. I make kimchi, which, as Callum's now heard, sometimes explodes.
A: Explodes?
B: In the jar. Fermentation. It went all up the cupboard and my daughter thought it was the best thing that'd ever happened.
A: Ah. Your daughter did the dog drawing, I think. In your photo.
B: She did, yeah, Isla, she's nine. She's campaigning for a dog. It's me and her in the week, so a dog feels like a lot right now.
A: Yes. It must be a lot already, on your own.
B: It is, sometimes, yeah. But she's great. So what about you, walking, anything like that?
A: Walking by the river. Swimming on Saturdays. And crochet. I'm slowly making a blanket.
B: Crochet's having such a moment, isn't it. There's a little shop in Stokes Croft that does classes. Have you been to any galleries or anything round you?
A: Not much. I went to the Ashmolean in Oxford. I enjoyed it more than I expected, actually.
B: Oh, that's a good one. I did that years ago with uni mates and we spent forever-
